scope: Proposition 3.10 (Reduction to strict data with a controlled rest end) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 18-19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (N, g, K) satisfy the exterior hypotheses of Theorem 2.2, including θ+ ≤ 0 on its smooth compact boundary, and let m = (E2 − |P|2)1/2 > 0. There is a sequence of smooth exterior data (gj, Kj) on N with the following properties: (i) µj > |Jj|gj everywhere and θ+,j < 0 on B. The constraint densities are integrable. On the end their DEC margin is bounded below by cjr−3−δ for some cj > 0 and one fixed 0 < δ < 1. (ii) Kj is compactly supported, and in a rest chart gj − δ = Ok(r−1) and Rgj = Ok(r−3−δ) for every k. In particular Ricgj = O(r−3) there. Their ADM momentum is zero. SPACETIME PENROSE INEQUALITIES 19 (iii) (gj, Kj) → (g, K) smoothly on every fixed compact subset up to the boundary, their ADM energies satisfy Ej → m, and agj (B) → ag(B). Consequently it suffices to prove the energy/enclosing-area inequality for the class in (i)–(ii) in order to prove Theorem 2.2 in its stated class.
